title: feat(studio): a permission set opens full-screen at its metadata address; the sharing overview gets its own route
body:
Fixes #36905

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：管理员在 Studio 里点开一个权限集，右侧整块显示权限矩阵，左上角 × 回到权限集列表，页签里能看引用、历史和源码；「谁能看到哪些记录」有了自己的页面，在左侧菜单「访问」里；旧书签自动跳到新地址。
- 为什么做：Studio 重构专题里「权限集矩阵全屏、默认共享总览独立」这一项，让权限集和其他元数据一样从列表点开、全屏编辑。
- 出错会怎样：有未保存修改时点 ×、切菜单、刷新或关标签页会先问（浏览器后退键不问）；AI 留下的草稿有提示并可一键放弃；本改动可以直接撤回。
- 要你做什么：这个改动超过 3,000 行（主要是删掉旧的权限侧栏和只为它服务的测试），按您的安排开发完等您审核合入。

## What changes

A permission set now opens full-screen at its metadata address, and the organization-wide default sharing overview has a route of its own. The Access pillar draws no page any more: every address it answered redirects.

Three facts for the reviewer, up front:

- **No published string is removed.** The 15 studio catalogue rows only the pillar read (`engine.studio.access.*` of its rail and create dialog, and `engine.studio.owd.railLabel`, en and zh) ship in the released `@object-ui/i18n`, so they stay in `ui/packages/i18n/src/namespaces/studio/en.ts` and `zh.ts`, byte-for-byte as on `main`, unread. `check:i18n-dead-keys` lists them as candidates (report only), as it does other unread rows.
- **Merged with #37108** (⌘K on every Studio design page): `origin/main` is merged at `709d2c1e`, and #37108's palette and ⌘K pins now expect the set's address and the overview's route.
- **The browser's Back button is not guarded** (epic #36890 decision 12): ×, ‹ ›, the left menu, ⌘K, Back to app, a reload and a tab close ask before unsaved edits are dropped; Back does not.

1. **The set's full-screen page** (`StudioPermissionSetPage`, new). On a package's leg, `/studio/PACKAGE/metadata/permission/NAME` opens the matrix (`PermissionMatrixEditPage`, its Studio presentation) in the area instead of sending the set to the Access pillar (`AREA_DESIGNER_PAGE_TYPES` / `areaItemOpensDesignerPage` in `metadataArea.ts`). The header is the full-screen detail's (`ResourceDetailHeader`, from #36892/#36901): × back to the list with its context, ‹ › through it, label (the machine name on its tooltip), type and package, ⋯. The tab row is the matrix's five sections, then `ItemToolTabs`' References, History (with the audit log) and Source; a tool tab is addressable (`?tab=`) and keeps the matrix mounted and hidden. The matrix gains one optional seam for this, `studio.frame` (`renderHeader`, `toolOpen`, `toolPanel`, `onDraftChangesRead`); without it the matrix draws its own header exactly as before. The cross-package leg (`/studio/~all/...`) keeps the matrix's environment page.
2. **What the pillar drew around the matrix comes along.** Discard draft, Explain access, the suggested-audience strip, and on a read-only base "New similar": in ⋯ on the page, and as a row action on the base's own rows in the list of sets (`ResourceListPage`; not on its pair's rows). The copy opens at its own metadata address with the strip saying where it landed (`permissionNewSimilar.tsx`, shared by the page and the list). Unsaved edits: the matrix registers with the shell's leave guard and the top bar's Save, so ×, ‹ ›, the menu, a reload and a tab close ask first; the browser's Back is not guarded (epic decisions 1 and 12). A discard sends a never-published set back to the list only when the package's sets were read and it is not among them: an unanswered read keeps the page on the set.
3. **Card item 6, decided here.** An AI-written pending draft (copilot or MCP) gets the designers' notice (`StudioAiDraftNotice`) with 「放弃 AI 的改动」, which drops that one set's draft at its package and asks first only when the matrix holds unsaved edits: the rule #37026 applied to the generic item page. A person's own leftover draft keeps Discard draft (decision 14). The matrix reports the draft's `draftChanges` from the read it already makes; no new request. Issue #36660 stays open: this PR applies its rule on the permission set page only; hooks, added actions and the sharing overview's rows are still its scope.
4. **The sharing overview's own route**, `/studio/PACKAGE/owd` (`StudioOwdOverviewPage`, new; `studioOwdOverviewPath`, `STUDIO_OWD_SECTION`), the Access group's menu entry (`studioMenuModel.ts`: its `to` and the current-entry mapping). A set's per-object visibility badge opens it on that object (`?object=NAME`). Its one read-only mark is the header's (objectui#12453), so the panel's own duplicate is gone.
5. **Address switch.** `permission` leaves `STUDIO_ITEM_PILLAR`, so `studioItemPath` (the palette, the AI artifact links, every producer) answers the metadata address; the menu's designer types are named explicitly so a permission set keeps its entry. `/studio/PACKAGE/access?surface=permission:NAME` redirects to the set's address, `?surface=owd:overview` to the overview, a bare `/access` to the list of sets, other parameters kept (`accessPillarRedirect.ts`). A set a read-only base's `.custom` pair adds (every "New similar" copy among them) was listed on the base's pillar and opened at the pair, writable, while the address named the base: its old address now opens at the pair's, `/studio/PAIR/metadata/permission/NAME?package=PAIR`. For an address that names a set, `AccessPillarLanding` (`accessPillarLanding.tsx`, new) reads the base's and the pair's sets, published and draft, as the pillar listed them, and `accessPillarSetHolder` decides: the base when it holds the name, else the pair when it does, else the base; a failed pair read lists none of the pair's sets, a failed base read stays on the base. The pair is the spec's pairing rule (`customizationPackageId`), as the list of sets derives it. Every other address redirects at once. `.../permission/NAME/history` opens the History tab: `AreaHistoryRedirect`'s own-editor exemption no longer covers a designer page. The address table's rows say where each moved (`redirectsTo`).
6. **The copilot keeps its context.** The pillar put the set in `?surface=`; the page's address carries it in the path, so the copilot's surface context reads a designer page's address too (`areaDesignerItemOf`, pillar `metadata`), and the page reports its label, so the chip still reads 「正在看：权限 · 组织成员」 (objectstack#35018). Only designer-page types are read this way, and `PACKAGE/metadata/permission/new` (the area's create page) is no item; every other area item is unchanged.
7. **Card item 5: the Access pillar and its rail are deleted** (`AccessPillar.tsx`, maintainer's answer on epic #36890, comment 7145880574: this card, reviewed by the maintainer as Tier H by size). Five test files go with it (`accessCreateTaken-26836`, `accessGuard`, `accessRailLabelLive-26846`, `accessRailLabels-11862`, `accessTabs-12456`), and the Access cases of `StudioRail.noMatches-26733`, `emptyStates-12514`, `readOnlyWording-11781`. Not all of that was pillar-only: `accessTabs-12456`'s matrix cases (the five tabs and sections, the facet panels kept mounted for the Save gate, the bulk strip with keyboard focus, the CRUD write, the sharing chip and the object count) and `accessCreateTaken-26836`'s discard cases (a declined question, a never-published set, a read-only package) moved to the page's pin; what went is the rail, the pillar's own header and its create dialog. The other pins of behaviour that lives on moved to the page too: the matrix's Studio Save (`studioSave-36511`, `saveSurface-12725`), New similar (`accessNewSimilar-28573`, now through ⋯), the suggestions strip on a read-only package (`accessSuggestionsReadOnly-33158`), the zh wording (`accessWording-34795`), the status place (`statusPlace-12524`) and the read-only banner. The page keeps objectstack#34795's ruling: the set's machine name is the title's tooltip, so its header draws no API-name chip.

## Tests

<details><summary>New pins</summary>

- `StudioPermissionSetPage.fullScreen-36905.test.tsx` (26 in round 1): the detail header and no matrix header; section and tool tabs; a tool tab addressable and the matrix kept mounted; × to the list; Discard draft at the set's package, CONTROL none without a draft; a declined question discards nothing; a never-published set's question and its discard back to the list, CONTROL a published set stays and re-reads; no discard on a read-only package; an unanswered sets read keeps the AI discard on the set; the AI notice for copilot and mcp drafts and its discard without a question on a clean page, CONTROL a person's draft; New similar in ⋯ landing at the copy's address with the strip, the no-package answer, CONTROL none on a writable package; the matrix's five sections (order and landing, each section, facets kept mounted, the bulk strip on every row, keyboard focus, CRUD and the header's count, the sharing chip opening the overview on its object and the object count).
- `metadataAreaHost.scope-28561.test.tsx` (+4, "New similar" on a read-only base's rows): the base's row offers it and its pair's row does not; the copy opens at its metadata address in the package the clone door names; an answer naming no package opens nothing and says so; CONTROL a writable package offers none. The list's create button is queried by its new test id (`metadata-list-create`), not its label, which "New similar" no longer collides with.
- `accessPillarRedirect.test.ts` (7): set, overview, bare and unknown surfaces, parameters carried; a set held in the pair opens at the pair's address while the overview and the list stay on the base; the set name an address opens; the holder decision (the pair's set, CONTROL the base's own set even when the pair holds the name too, neither, a failed pair read, a failed base read).
- `StudioDesignSurface.accessPairCopy-29674.test.tsx` (+4, the retired pillar's address through the real surface): `/studio/BASE/access?surface=permission:COPY` lands on `/studio/PAIR/metadata/permission/COPY?package=PAIR`, the copy reads Custom and an edit saves at the pair; a set created in the pair, still a draft, lands there too; the address's other parameters reach the redirect and ride along (`?ref=bookmark`; `?changes=review` is consumed by the surface, which opens the drawer); CONTROL the base's own set's old address stays on the base and reads Package.
- `StudioPermissionSetPage.fullScreen-36905.test.tsx` (+3, the sharing chip's leave guard): with a dirty matrix the chip asks the unsaved-edits question once, and declined the page stays on the set with the edit; confirmed it opens the overview on its object; CONTROL a clean matrix asks nothing.
- `StudioMetadataArea.routes-28561.test.tsx` (+4): the set opens in place on writable and read-only packages, CONTROL the cross-package leg keeps the generic page, the old history address opens the History tab.
- `metadataArea.test.ts`, `studioAddress.test.ts`, `studioMenuModel.test.ts`: the predicate, the address reader (the create page is no item), `studioOwdOverviewPath`, the moved rows agree with the redirect, the menu entry and current key.

</details>

<details><summary>Pins moved to the new addresses</summary>

- From #37108 after the merge: `StudioDesignSurface.metadataArea-28561` (⌘K's Default sharing from a set's page opens `/studio/PACKAGE/owd`), `StudioPaletteGroups.surfaceScope-36900` (an item opens at `/studio/PACKAGE/metadata/permission/NAME?package=PACKAGE`, the menu entry at `/studio/PACKAGE/owd`), `studioPaletteModel-36900` (leave, re-enter and stay read on the set's address; the overview's route is a leave).
- `StudioRoute.metadataArea-28561` (console): the Studio gate refuses `/studio/PACKAGE/owd` as it refuses the old overview address.
- `StudioDesignSurface.pillarNavGuard.test.tsx`: decision 12 on the set page and the overview page (menu, Back to app, the shell seam; dirty matrix and dirty overview rows; CONTROL clean).
- `StudioDesignSurface.accessPairCopy-29674.test.tsx`: a pair's copy at the pair's address lists the base's objects, saves at the pair, names the base by its label, reads Custom; CONTROL the base's own set. Its docstring now claims only the header's half it reads.
- `StudioItemHeader.statusPlace-12524`: the read-only link is a direct child of the page's action group, the group a direct child of the actions slot.
- `StudioDesignSurface.aiChipLabel.test.tsx`: the chip and the agent's surface context on the set page.
- `accessSegment-12452`: the old Access address lands on the list of sets with its entry current. `notFound-26708`, `readOnlyPosture-12453`, `pillarsClaimSlot-12725`, `rightSlot-12725`, `backToApp-36501`, `changesCount-11787`, `copilotDraftBadge-12725`, `publishPosture-12517` used the Access pillar as "a package page that claims nothing"; they use the overview page now.

</details>

<details><summary>Ablations (four, each reverted)</summary>

- Round 1: `const aiDraft = …` forced to `false` through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: anchor 1 → 0, blob `3dc44aa6` → `fdd76cfd`; the AI-draft describe went 2 failed, 1 passed (the CONTROL); restored blob == HEAD `3dc44aa6`, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- This round, on `11aaddcc`: the never-published test put back to `!read?.published.has(name)` through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: anchor 1 → 0, blob `3ac18e32` → `0923112b`; the page's discard cases went 1 failed (the unanswered-read pin), 9 passed (the published CONTROL among them); restored blob == HEAD `3ac18e32`, `git diff HEAD` empty. A first pass on `3d7c1d00` stayed green: the pin asserted the address right after the reset and raced the navigation, so it now waits for the re-read only a page that stays makes.
- Round 3, on `7d5d87bd` (tree identical to `79987757`): the landing's holder ignored (`{ setHeldIn: holder ?? packageId }` → `{ setHeldIn: packageId }` in `accessPillarLanding.tsx`) through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: anchor 1 → 0, blob `f9502964` → `169d7fcc`; `accessPairCopy-29674` went 3 failed (the copy, the pair's draft, the carried query), 8 passed (the base's CONTROL among them); restored blob == HEAD `f9502964`, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- Round 3, on `7d5d87bd`: the chip's guard removed (`confirmUnsavedLeave(() => navigate(…))` → a bare `navigate(…)` in `StudioPermissionSetPage.tsx`) through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: anchor 1 → 0, blob `3ac18e32` → `2b68c388`; `fullScreen-36905` went 2 failed (declined and confirmed both ask once), 27 passed (the clean CONTROL among them); restored blob == HEAD `3ac18e32`, `git diff HEAD` empty. A first spelling was refused by the tool before anything ran (its replacement was a substring of the anchor, so the replacement count could not rise).

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- `StudioDesignSurface`'s `PILLAR_FOR_SURFACE_TYPE` still routes a `permission` surface request through `/access?surface=`, and its "open Access" toast action through bare `/access`; both now land via the redirect. They go with the pillar routes in #36909.
- `PermissionMatrixEditor`'s Studio header without a `frame` (its own `StudioItemHeader`, History button and ⋯) has no Studio host since the pillar is gone; 13 of the matrix's own unit tests still render it, so it stays this round and its doc comments say so. Deleting it with those tests' rewrite goes with #36909. The matrix's prop docs no longer name the Access pillar as their host.
- On a pair's leg the provenance chip reads Custom for every set (`customizationMark: 'added'`): a permission set takes no override (ADR-0005), so a set the pair holds is one it adds.
- The suggested-audience strip draws on every set page, as it drew above every set in the pillar.
- `node scripts/pm/overlap-check.mjs` on `7d5d87bd` (tree identical to `79987757`): `origin/main` (`3b4f0b98`) merges cleanly; #37185 merges cleanly; #37168 and #37169 (open) conflict on `StudioAiCopilot.tsx`, `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`, `StudioMetadataArea.tsx`, `metadataArea.ts`, `studioAddress.ts`, `studioMenuModel.ts` and their tests; #37166 now conflicts on `StudioDesignSurface.notFound-26708.test.tsx`, a file this round does not touch. Whichever lands second rebases.
- The seat's L1 REWORK (7150986891) on the contract review (7150969735): M1 fixed (item 5, pinned in `accessPairCopy-29674` and `accessPillarRedirect.test.ts`, ablated); S1 fixed (the chip's dirty-matrix cases, ablated); N1 fixed (the carried-query case through the real surface). The pair redirect reads the spec's pairing rule rather than the surface's `pairId`: that value is set only once the package list and its manifests answer, and a failed manifests read leaves it unset, which would hold the redirect forever.
- Review nits from the seat's L1 (7147848289): N1 above; N2, N3, N4, N7, N8 and N10 fixed in the pins and comments named in Tests; N5 fixed (`areaDesignerItemOf` reads `permission/new` as no item); N6 fixed and pinned (the unanswered-read case, ablated above); N9 in item 3.
